title: Encoded value after ApiKey in an Authorization header
summary: A synthetic encoded API key after the ApiKey scheme in an Authorization or Proxy-Authorization header, in a raw request, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map, including a lowercase header name and scheme.
rationale: Elastic documents the encoded value as the credential sent after the ApiKey scheme. The scheme name is not unique to Elastic, and the carrier cannot tell a Cloud or Serverless key from a self-managed one, so the attribution stays generic. The encoded value is covered whole: it is not decoded and no alphabet or width is assumed. The header name, scheme and closing quote are outside the extent.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#232). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the value after an explicit ApiKey scheme in Authorization or Proxy-Authorization is treated as a credential and covered whole, consistent with how the other authorization credentials are handled. Elastic documents the scheme as the carrier of the encoded value (carrier existence only); the boundary, value admission, extent and generic authorization attribution are the project's decisions.

sources.supports: You must create an API key and use the encoded value in the request header: Authorization: ApiKey ${API_KEY}

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
